correctness.rationale: For odd prime powers q and every nonzero fixed radius parameter t, the norm conic has S=q-chi(-1) points and antipodal pairs. Distinct equal-radius circles intersect in at most two points; for a pair on one circle the other potential center is a+b-c, coinciding exactly for antipodes. Hence all point pairs sharing a circle are shattered, and triples are shattered exactly when concyclic and without antipodal pairs; their unique common center and alternative pair centers provide all traces (small q cases separately). Count center-pair incidence once/twice and nonantipodal triples to get s2=q²S²/4, s3=q²S(S-2)(S-4)/6, no degree>=4 by unique center through a triple. Independent exhaustive center-bitset calculations for q=3,5,7,11,t=1 returned (S,s2,s3)=(4,36,0),(4,100,0),(8,784,1568),(12,4356,19360). Proof covers all odd prime powers and nonzero t.
